description.value: This study investigated the effects of opioid blockade, via naltrexone, on functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) measures during methamphetamine cue-reactivity in individuals with methamphetamine use disorder.

spans.text: The present study investigated the effects of opioid blockade, via naltrexone, on functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) measures during methamphetamine cue-reactivity to elucidate the role of endogenous opioids in the neural systems underlying drug craving.

description.value: A randomized, placebo controlled, within-subjects protocol involving two 3-day medication administrations, naltrexone and placebo, with MRI scanning on the third day.

spans.text: Twenty-four medically eligible non-treatment-seeking individuals with a methamphetamine use disorder completed a within-subjects protocol that involved the completion of two, 3-day medication administrations (naltrexone/placebo; medication order randomized between subjects) and an MRI scan on the third day

description.value: Naltrexone administered for 3 days, with 25 mg on day one and 50 mg on days two and three.

spans.text: Participants received a 25 mg dose on day one and 50 mg doses on days two and three in the naltrexone condition

description.value: Color-matched placebo pills administered for 3 days.

recruitment_method.value: Recruitment of non-treatment-seeking individuals with methamphetamine use disorder; 16 participants were recruited through a 7-day inpatient protocol and 8 through an intensive outpatient protocol.

spans.text: Sixteen participants were scanned prior to laboratory testing as part of a 7-day inpatient protocol investigating the effects of naltrexone on subjective response to methamphetamine administration ( Ray et al , 2015a ) and the remaining eight participants were administered the medication daily on an intensive outpatient basis.

medication_status.value: Within-subject randomized medication conditions; participants received naltrexone or matched placebo for 3 days, with scanning on day 3 at the target dose. Participants were abstinent from alcohol and substances during study periods.

spans.text: Participants received a 25 mg dose on day one and 50 mg doses on days two and three in the naltrexone condition, and color-matched placebo pills in the placebo condition

description.value: fMRI data were motion corrected, brain extracted, smoothed, high-pass filtered, registered to structural images, and transformed into standard MNI space.
